summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, coronary artery disease, and peripheral vascular disease, was admitted with worsening dyspnea on exertion, chest pressure, and significant lower extremity and abdominal swelling. He had recently been discharged after treatment for volume overload and DVT. Evaluation revealed acute on chronic diastolic heart failure with volume overload, confirmed by elevated BNP, chest imaging, and physical findings. He was treated with IV furosemide, transitioned to oral torsemide 60 mg daily, and had his tacrolimus increased to maintain therapeutic levels. A cardiac catheterization showed chronic total occlusion of the RCA and mild LAD disease, not requiring intervention. Carotid ultrasound revealed complete occlusion of the right internal carotid artery and 60-69% stenosis on the left, with outpatient vascular follow-up planned. His INR was subtherapeutic on admission, requiring heparin bridging until warfarin achieved therapeutic effect. He was also started on potassium supplementation for hypokalemia. By discharge, his symptoms improved, weight decreased from 92.9 kg to 89.5 kg, and he was stable on adjusted medications with follow-up arranged.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Occlusion and stenosis of bilateral carotid arteries
Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
